reason: The cited evidence (E2) confirms Cr-V-rich precipitate formation in the baseline alloy at 8 dpa, but provides no data on Hf substitution, its effect on segregation kinetics, diffusion, phase stability, or manufacturability. The hypothesis relies on unsupported mechanistic assumptions about Hf behavior.
premises: Cr-V-rich precipitates form in nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 at ~8 dpa
Hf substitution reduces Cr-V co-segregation and precipitate nucleation
Hf has slower diffusion kinetics than Cr at defect sinks
The modified alloy retains a stable single-phase nanocrystalline structure
Bulk manufacturability is not compromised by the Hf substitution
